newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: FOCUS-Murdoch garage sale continues apace.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Murdoch garage sale continues apace.

text.p: The cash register at Rupert Murdoch's garage sale of non-core assets from his global media group rang to the tune of another A$325 million on Wednesday when News Corp sold its 40 percent stake in PMP Communications.
The sale of News' interests in the Australian multi-media group brings the total raised in the asset sale programme to A$642.5 million (US$478 million) since early June.
This is just over half the US$800 million in asset sales flagged by Murdoch to an analysts briefing in Los Angeles on May 8 after News' released its third financial quarter results.

Murdoch's aggressive expansion over the last three years into U.S. movies, network television and satellite television has forced News to raise cash this year to soothe market and rating agency concerns about rising debt levels.
News announced last week the sale of its 50 percent stake in Australian Newsprint Mills (ANM) to New Zealand's Fletcher Challenge Paper Ltd for A$293.5 million.
Last month News also announced it had sold 18.6 percent of Australian computer services group Computer Power Group Ltd for A$24 million.

Analysts said News' sale of 101.6 million shares in PMP at A$3.20 a share to institutional investors through Were Stockbroking on Wednesday showed it was serious about selling poorly-performing assets in low growth media sectors.
They said ratings agencies were likely to welcome the continued asset sale programme.

"There was a need to satisfy the financial community's concerns in terms of gearing and so it's been disposing of some of its peripheral assets like Australian Newsprint Mills and Pacific Magazines (PMP) locally, and more odds and sods will follow," said ANZ Investment Banking media analyst Bob Peters.
"They're under pressure from the ratings agencies and they need to be seen to be heading in the right direction," said another media analyst.
News was reminded of the delicacy of its ratings position on June 12 when Standard & Poors Corp put News' BBB corporate credit rating on creditwatch with negative implications.

The warning came after News announced the US$1.9 billion purchase of International Family Entertainment, a U.S. family cable television group, and the US$1.1 billion sale of its U.S. satellite television assets to the Primestar consortium for convertible Primestar notes and stock -- not cash.
News is keen to avoid a rating downgrade to BBB-minus as its debt would then fall to just one step above the BB junk bond category.
"Further progress with asset sales to reduce debt could result in an affirmation," Standard & Poors said in June.
Analyst opinion remained divided about the PMP sale and whether News was selling a strong media asset for a song or getting out of a sluggish performer at a reasonable price.
"They've gotten out cheap. It's an excellent deal for the institutions," said one media analyst.

PMP owns several successful magazines, including the Australian version of TV Week and women's magazine New Idea, and controls a listed multi-media group called Shomega Ltd SHO.AX which manufactures compact discs and is an electronic publisher.
But PMP has lagged the overall market since News sold over 50 percent of it for A$3.20 a share in a 1992 float.
PMP closed down 46 cents at A$3.19 on Wednesday.
In February PMP, once known as Pacific Magazines, posted a lower first half year net profit of A$30.55 million on sales of A$588.53 million.
Only last month it downgraded its profit forecast for the full year to June 30, 1997, citing a slow economy and unprofitable printing operations.
"It hasn't been a great story. Few people like the stock," said Neil Franklin, a broker at HSBC James Capel.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
